opening: What happens when you've done everything you can, yet the outcome remains beyond your control? Sometimes the greatest change isn't in our circumstances, but in the weight we no longer feel compelled to carry. A reflection on faith, unanswered prayers, St. Jude's intercession, and the surprising lesson hidden in Jesus' parable of the dishonest steward.

Jesus tells us in Matthew 11:

“Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.”

And then:

“For my yoke is easy, and my burden light.”

I have heard these words so many times. But I think I am only now beginning to understand them.

Jesus doesn't promise that we will never have difficulties. He doesn't tell us that every dispute will be resolved in our favor or that every prayer will receive the answer we want.

He invites us to carry our burdens differently.

I used to think that if I worried enough, worked hard enough, or anticipated every possible problem, I might somehow protect myself from an unfavorable outcome.

But worry does not give me control over tomorrow.

It only takes away some of the peace available to me today.

And perhaps that is the burden Jesus is helping me put down.

Today's first reading offers another reminder. Paul tells us that our citizenship is in heaven.

We live in this world, and we have responsibilities within it. We must make decisions, protect what has been entrusted to us, and exercise good judgment. But our lives are not ultimately defined by the disputes we win, the money we recover, or the difficulties we manage to overcome.

Our hope rests somewhere greater.

I can pursue what is fair without allowing the struggle to consume me.

I can ask for help without believing that I have failed.

I can pray for a particular outcome while accepting that God's care for me does not depend on receiving it.

And I can continue searching for solutions without surrendering my peace to uncertainty.

Perhaps that is what I am learning from the dishonest steward after all.

Not to imitate his dishonesty, but to recognize the importance of prudence while remembering that my security does not rest entirely upon my own cleverness.

I want to do what is right, use the abilities God has given me, and remain faithful in the decisions I make.

But I no longer want to carry the fear of everything that might happen.

I can be responsible for my efforts without believing I must control the outcome.

That is a freedom I am only beginning to experience.

And what a relief it is to discover that trusting God does not mean I have to stop working.

It means I can finally stop worrying that everything depends on me.
prayer: Lord Jesus,  You know the burdens I carry, the uncertainties I face, and how often I try to find answers through my own strength.  Thank You for the wisdom to recognize the possibilities before me and the courage to pursue what is right.  Teach me to be prudent without becoming consumed by my circumstances. Help me to remain honest, fair, and faithful, even when the world around me seems to operate differently.  And when I have done what I reasonably can, help me release the outcome into Your hands.  St. Jude, faithful apostle and patron of desperate causes, I ask for your continued intercession. Pray that I may recognize God's guidance, persevere when necessary, and find peace when the answers are beyond my control.  Jesus, You have promised rest to those who are burdened.  Teach me what it means to accept Your yoke and trust in Your care.  May I never confuse worrying with responsibility, or surrendering my fears with surrendering my faith.  Let me do my part with integrity and leave what remains in Your hands.  Amen.
theme: Finding peace through faith while facing life's uncertainties, learning to act with wisdom without surrendering our integrity, and discovering the freedom of trusting God with what we cannot control.
title: Dishonest Prudence
